# Results — Study 493 (New-Highs-New-Lows breadth)

*Generated by [`examples/verify.py`](../examples/verify.py). The believers' claim — **breadth
leads price: a surge of net new 52-week highs (a "breadth thrust") forecasts the index** —
encoded as a mechanical rule. Each day we count basket members at a fresh 252-day (52-week)
high minus those at a fresh low, divide by the basket size, smooth over 10 days, and fire a long
on SPY when that NH-NL line crosses up through +0.20; entry is at the **next close** (one
documented lag), and we measure the forward 5/10/20/60-day return. Offline & deterministic once
cached; run `python examples/verify.py` to reproduce every number.*

## Data stamp

| Field | Value |
|---|---|
| Real tape | yfinance daily adjusted (**total-return**) closes; breadth proxied by **SPY, QQQ, IWM, DIA, GLD** (public, no key) |
| Window | 2005-01-03 → 2026-05-29 (**As-of 2026-05-31**, partial June dropped; **21.4** years) |
| SPY fingerprint | `4cb5244f3990` (sha1[:12] of the close column, As-of slice) |
| Entries | **114** mechanical breadth thrusts on SPY (52-week extremes, 10-day smoothed line, +0.20 up-cross) |
| Timing / costs | extremes use **trailing 252 bars only** (no look-ahead); enter the **next close** (one lag); hold 5/10/20/60 days; **1 bp** one-way × 2 legs per thrust |

> **Breadth proxy — this caps the test.** A *true* new-highs/new-lows reading (the NYSE NH-NL
> that IBD and the Hindenburg-Omen literature use) counts **thousands** of listed issues. We
> cannot fetch that offline, so we proxy breadth with a small basket of **5 liquid ETFs** spanning
> the broad tape, big-cap tech, small caps, large caps and gold. A 5-name basket has far less
> cross-sectional resolution than a real advance/decline universe — this is a **coarse proxy**.
> The Signal axis is unchanged: does the breadth thrust beat a **random-day** entry on SPY?

> **Price-only vs total-return.** The ETFs are auto-adjusted (dividends reinvested) — labelled
> total-return everywhere. The random-entry control neutralizes the drift baseline, which is the
> only thing a single-instrument breadth-timing study turns on.

## The signal — breadth thrust vs a drift-matched random baseline (the honest test)

One-sample *t* is the **misleading** number (it measures the index's upward drift, and breadth
is mechanically high *after* a rally); the **Welch thrust-vs-random** *t* is the test that
matters. Δ = thrust − random.

| horizon | n | thrust | win% | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (thrust−random) | net of cost | Welch *t* | *p* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| 5-day  | 113 | +5.7 bps   | 54% | +0.45 | +39.7 bps  | **−34.0 bps** | +3.7 bps   | −1.09 | 0.275 |
| 10-day | 113 | +26.3 bps  | 65% | +1.39 | +84.6 bps  | **−58.2 bps** | +24.3 bps  | −1.48 | 0.142 |
| 20-day | 113 | +36.3 bps  | 66% | +1.29 | +125.1 bps | **−88.8 bps** | +34.3 bps  | −1.51 | 0.132 |
| 60-day | 112 | +187.4 bps | 74% | +2.94 | +274.0 bps | **−86.7 bps** | +185.4 bps | −0.92 | 0.358 |

Read it carefully. The one-sample *t* against zero looks respectable (**+2.94** at 60 days) — but
that is **pure beta**: long-only entries on an upward-drifting index inherit the drift, and a
breadth thrust by construction flags "the market just went up." Against the **drift-matched
random baseline**, the breadth thrust is *worse* at **every** horizon (Δ = −34.0 / −58.2 / −88.8
/ −86.7 bps). The thrust-minus-random Welch *t* is **negative throughout** (max −0.92 at 60 days)
— never close to the desk's *t* ≥ 2 bar, and on the *wrong side*. The NH-NL line does not lead.

## Per-index (H = 20) — the thrust loses to random everywhere

Trading each basket member on the *same* breadth line:

| index | entries | thrust | one-sample *t* | random | Δ (thrust−random) |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY | 114 | +36.3 bps  | +1.29 | +125.1 bps | **−88.8 bps** |
| QQQ | 114 | +44.1 bps  | +1.49 | +119.3 bps | **−75.2 bps** |
| IWM | 114 | −13.4 bps  | −0.33 | +185.6 bps | **−199.0 bps** |
| DIA | 114 | +41.3 bps  | +1.32 | +141.9 bps | **−100.6 bps** |
| GLD | 114 | +128.0 bps | +2.58 | +127.5 bps | **+0.4 bps** |

Only **GLD** is a wash (+0.4 bps); every equity index is deeply negative, with IWM the worst at
−199 bps behind random. No coherent cross-sectional edge — the hallmark of relabelled drift.

## Breadth-structure placebo — scramble membership, nothing changes

The decisive "does the aggregation matter?" test: permute, **per member across time**, which
days each member prints a new high — keeping every member's marginal new-high rate but destroying
the cross-sectional co-movement that makes a genuine breadth thrust. If price genuinely respected
*the real breadth aggregation*, the scramble would collapse the result.

| test | observed breadth-thrust 20d return | placebo *p* | draws |
|---|--:|--:|--:|
| SPY shuffled-membership breadth | +36.3 bps | **0.818** | 500 |

**82% of scrambled-breadth lines match or beat the real one** (*p* = 0.818). The NH-NL
aggregation carries no information — structural nonsense does just as well. "Breadth leads the
index" is busted.

## Synthetic positive control — the harness CAN bank a real lead

On a deterministic basket with a *planted* breadth-lead (knob `edge` — today's breadth drifts the
index over the next H days), the same thrust rule behaves exactly as it must — so the flat
real-tape result is a genuine "nothing there", not a dead detector.

| planted lead | n | thrust | win% | one-sample *t* |
|---|--:|--:|--:|--:|
| **0.00** (no lead) | 16 | −53.3 bps | 44% | −0.75 |
| **0.60** (real planted lead) | 16 | +364.4 bps | 88% | **+3.02** |

With no planted lead the control sits at *t* ≈ 0 (no false positive); a real planted lead lights
up at *t* = +3.02 with an 88% win-rate. The detector is live.

## Verdict

- **Signal — NONE.** The breadth thrust does **not** beat a drift-matched random baseline (thrust
  − random = −34.0 / −58.2 / −88.8 / −86.7 bps at 5/10/20/60 days; the thrust-vs-random Welch *t*
  is negative at every horizon). The one-sample *t*'s (60-day +2.94) are pure beta — the upward
  drift of long equity indices, plus breadth's mechanical lag behind price.
- **Tradability — MIRAGE.** There is no residual edge once the drift you were always getting is
  removed, and the thrust actually *underperforms* random entries. The same drift is captured more
  cheaply and more fully by holding the index; the breadth rule trades less and pays costs on each
  thrust. No capacity question because there is no edge to scale.
- **"Breadth leads the index"? — BUSTED.** The shuffled-membership placebo leaves the result
  intact (*p* = 0.818): structural-nonsense breadth lines do as well as the real one, so the NH-NL
  aggregation carries no forecasting information. The new-highs/new-lows line is a descriptive
  market-internals gauge, not a forecasting strategy.

> **Caveat.** Breadth here is a 5-ETF proxy, not a true thousands-issue NH-NL universe. The
> failure is lopsided enough (loses to random at every horizon; placebo *p* ≈ 0.82) that a richer
> basket would have to overturn a very clear result — but a real advance/decline feed is the
> obvious follow-up.
